stem: A legal team has collected 400,000 emails for a case and wants to cut review time by grouping textually similar documents and keeping only the messages that give the full context of each email thread. Which eDiscovery capability provides this?

choices.text: Search and delete, which removes the duplicate messages from the mailboxes across the organization.
Search statistics, which estimate the number and size of matching items and the locations with the most results.
A hold on the content locations, which preserves every item in the mailboxes until the case is closed.
Premium eDiscovery analytics on a review set, including near duplicate detection and email threading.

stem: An IT administrator needs to find out which user deleted a shared document from a SharePoint site two months ago. No special configuration was done beforehand. Which Microsoft Purview capability can answer this?

choices.text: Audit (Standard), which is enabled by default and keeps searchable audit records of user and admin activity for 180 days.
A retention policy for the site, which records the name of each user who deletes a file in a property of the document.
Insider risk analytics, which evaluates potential insider risks in the organization without any configured policies.
Content explorer, which shows the current snapshot of labeled items and the SharePoint site where each item is stored.

stem: Investigators of a suspected mailbox compromise need to know which specific email messages an attacker read, and they want audit records for Exchange, SharePoint and Microsoft Entra ID kept longer than 180 days. Which TWO capabilities of Audit (Premium) address these needs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Encryption of every mailbox the attacker accessed so that the messages can no longer be read by anyone.
A hold that preserves the compromised mailbox contents until an eDiscovery case for it has been closed.
A default one-year retention of Exchange, SharePoint and Microsoft Entra audit records, with custom policies.
Automatic blocking of the attacker's sign-ins as soon as a suspicious MailItemsAccessed record is logged.
Intelligent insights such as the MailItemsAccessed event, which records when mail items were accessed.

stem: A regulated company has Audit (Premium) and must keep the audit records of a group of finance users for ten years. Which statement about meeting this requirement is correct?

choices.text: A retention label applied to the finance users' mailboxes keeps their audit records for the period set on that label.
An audit log retention policy for those users is needed, and each user needs the 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on license.
Exporting the audit search to a CSV file once extends the retention of those records in the audit log to ten years.
Audit (Standard) already keeps every audit record for ten years, so no extra configuration or license is required.

stem: A company wants to use insider risk management but is unsure which types of risky activity are most common among its users and which policies to configure first. Which capability helps before any policies exist?

choices.text: Audit log retention policies, which keep the records of risky users for ten years so that trends can be studied later.
The Data leaks policy template, which must be enabled for every user before any risk information can be collected.
Insider risk analytics, which evaluates potential insider risks across the organization without configuring policies.
Content explorer, which lists all labeled files so that administrators can guess which users are most likely to leak.

stem: A manufacturer runs a legacy app on Azure virtual machines, a new API on Azure App Service and its email on Microsoft 365. The board wants a single list of the security duties the company keeps in all three, so that no budget line is cut by mistake after the move. According to the shared responsibility model, which THREE responsibilities stay with the company in every one of these service models? (Select THREE)

choices.text: Protecting the physical hosts and datacenter network, because the company still chooses the Azure region that holds the workloads.
Patching the operating system of the servers that run each workload, because the company deploys the code that runs there.
Maintaining the web server and runtime middleware under each application, because the company chose which language framework to use.
Classifying and protecting the company's own data, including deciding what is sensitive and how it must be encrypted.
Securing the laptops, tablets and phones that employees use to connect to the cloud services and the company's data.
Managing user accounts, authentication methods and access permissions, such as requiring MFA and removing leavers' access.

stem: An insurer already has strong MFA for all staff and a firewall at its internet edge. A penetration test shows that once the testers controlled one web server, they could connect directly to every database server in the same flat network. The security lead wants to close this gap at the layer the testers exploited, without rewriting the applications. Which defense-in-depth control addresses that specific layer?

choices.text: Divide the network into separate zones for web and database servers and allow only the required ports between those zones.
Turn on encryption at rest for every database file so that stolen disks or backups cannot be read by anyone outside the company.
Add DDoS protection in front of the public endpoints so that large floods of attack traffic are filtered before they arrive.
Require phishing-resistant authentication methods for every administrator who signs in to the web or database servers.

stem: A retailer rewrites its access rules. First, every request to a business app must be evaluated using the user's identity, location and device health, even when the device is on the office network. Second, contractors will receive access to only the one app their contract covers, and only until the contract ends. Which TWO Zero Trust guiding principles do these two rules apply? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Assume breach, because the company minimizes blast radius by segmenting access and using analytics to detect threats as they happen.
Verify explicitly, because every access decision uses all available data points instead of the network the request came from.
Trust the corporate network, because devices that are already on the office network have passed the perimeter and need fewer checks.
Defense in depth, because the company adds a second firewall layer at the perimeter to stop contractors from reaching other apps.
Use least privilege access, because users get just-in-time and just-enough access that is limited both in scope and in time.

stem: A hospital's security team reviews five controls that protect its patient portal, which doctors, nurses and billing staff use daily. It wants to label each one correctly before an audit, because the auditor will test proof-of-identity controls separately from controls that decide what a proven identity may do. Which TWO of the following are authorization controls rather than authentication controls? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A password complexity rule that requires long passwords so that the identity proof users give at each sign-in is harder to guess.
A role assignment that gives the billing team read access to invoices in the portal's database only.
A one-time code from the Microsoft Authenticator app that a doctor enters after his password at each new sign-in.
A FIDO2 security key that a nurse touches after typing her user name, which proves she holds the registered key.
A SharePoint permission level that lets ward managers edit staffing documents but only view the policy documents.

stem: A biotech firm gives researchers from a partner university access to its lab-results web app. The university insists that its staff keep using their own university credentials, and the firm's legal team insists that the firm must never store or reset those people's passwords. When a researcher leaves the university, access must end without the firm doing anything. Which approach meets both demands?

choices.text: Synchronize the university's directory into the firm's on-premises Active Directory every night and let researchers sign in there.
Create local accounts in the firm's directory for each researcher and copy their current university passwords into them.
Issue one shared service account to the university's research group and rotate its password whenever a researcher leaves.
Set up federation so the firm's app trusts sign-in tokens issued by the university's identity provider for its own staff.

stem: A dev team's GitHub Actions workflow deploys infrastructure to Azure several times a day. Today it signs in with a client secret stored in the repository's secrets, and auditors flagged that the secret has not been rotated in two years. The team wants no long-lived secret anywhere and does not want to run its build agents inside Azure. Which Microsoft Entra capability meets these needs?

choices.text: Create a dedicated user account for the pipeline, exclude it from MFA, and store its password in an Azure Key Vault that the workflow reads.
Replace the client secret with a certificate credential on the app registration and store the private key as a repository secret.
Configure workload identity federation so an app registration or user-assigned managed identity trusts GitHub-issued workflow tokens.
Assign a system-assigned managed identity to the GitHub repository so that Azure issues tokens to the workflow without any secret.

stem: A logistics startup opens a new branch with forty corporate-owned Windows laptops. It has no on-premises servers or domain controllers anywhere, and IT wants staff to sign in to the laptops with their Microsoft Entra work accounts and get single sign-on to cloud apps. Devices must be manageable by the organization rather than personally owned. Which device identity option fits?

choices.text: Microsoft Entra joined, which joins organization-owned devices directly to Microsoft Entra ID for work-account sign-in.
Microsoft Entra hybrid joined, which joins the laptops to an on-premises domain first and then registers them with Microsoft Entra ID.
Microsoft Entra registered, which adds a work account to a personally owned device so the user can reach company apps and email.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services, which hosts managed domain controllers in Azure that the laptops must join over a site-to-site VPN.

stem: An engineering firm and a supplier both use Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Teams. They want to collaborate in a Teams shared channel where each side signs in with its own home account. The firm's identity team has one firm rule: supplier staff must not be added as guest user objects in the firm's directory. Which external collaboration capability fits?

choices.text: Cross-tenant synchronization, which automatically creates and updates supplier users as members of the firm's own Microsoft Entra tenant.
B2B direct connect, a mutual two-way trust for Teams shared channels in which external users are not added as guests.
Microsoft Entra External ID for customers, which creates a separate external tenant for consumer sign-up to public-facing applications.
B2B collaboration, which invites supplier staff as guest users so they can sign in to the firm's apps with their own credentials.

stem: A design agency uses Microsoft Entra ID Free with security defaults turned on, so every user gets MFA prompts. Staff complain about prompts at the office. Management wants MFA required only for sign-ins from outside the office's public IP range, while keeping costs as low as possible. Which change meets the requirement with the LEAST extra licensing?

choices.text: Keep security defaults and add the office IP range as an exclusion inside the security defaults settings so office sign-ins skip MFA.
Turn off security defaults and require users to register Windows Hello for Business, which removes the MFA prompts from every sign-in at once.
License Microsoft Entra ID P2 and add a sign-in risk policy that requires MFA whenever ID Protection rates a sign-in as risky.
License Entra ID P1, turn off security defaults, and add a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA outside the office's named location.

stem: A semiconductor plant bans personal and company phones on its clean-room floor. Operators sign in to shared terminals whose USB ports and NFC readers are disabled for contamination and security reasons, and each sign-in must still use a second factor. The security team wants a method that Microsoft Entra ID supports natively. Which second-factor method fits these constraints?

choices.text: FIDO2 security keys that operators insert into the terminal and touch to complete a phishing-resistant sign-in.
Microsoft Authenticator push notifications that operators approve by entering the number shown on the terminal screen.
OATH TOTP hardware tokens that display a new six-digit code every 30 or 60 seconds for the operator to type in.
SMS text messages with a one-time code sent to a mobile number that each operator registers during onboarding.

stem: A school district synchronizes staff accounts from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID. Teachers who forget their passwords call the help desk, which is overwhelmed in September. The district wants teachers to reset their own password from a browser at home, and the new password must also work the next morning on domain-joined classroom PCs. Which capability meets both requirements?

choices.text: Self-service password reset with password writeback, which writes the new password back to on-premises Active Directory.
Self-service password reset in cloud-only mode, which updates the password in Microsoft Entra ID for the synchronized account.
Microsoft Entra Password Protection with the on-premises agent, which blocks weak passwords when teachers change them.
A Temporary Access Pass issued by the help desk, which lets teachers sign in once and then register a new password themselves.

stem: A financial services company hires a security analyst who must review security reports, alerts and Secure Score across the Microsoft 365 tenant, and must also view (but never change) the Azure resources in the production subscription. Policy requires least privilege and no ability to modify any setting. Which TWO role assignments together meet the requirement? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The Azure Owner role at the production subscription scope, which lets the analyst view every resource and delegate access to colleagues.
The Microsoft Entra Security Administrator role, which lets the analyst read security reports and also manage security policies and settings.
The Azure Reader role assigned at the production subscription scope, which lets the analyst view every resource without changing anything.
The Microsoft Entra Global Reader role assigned at the production subscription scope, so it covers the subscription's Azure resources as well.
The Microsoft Entra Security Reader role, which grants read-only access to security information and reports across the tenant.

stem: A pharmaceutical company lets guest researchers from partner universities into a SharePoint project site. Legal requires that each guest accepts the company's confidentiality terms before the first access and whenever the terms change, and security requires MFA for every guest sign-in. The company already has Microsoft Entra ID P1. Which approach meets both requirements in one place?

choices.text: A sensitivity label on the project site that encrypts its files and shows the confidentiality terms as a header on each document.
A Conditional Access policy for guest users whose grant controls require MFA and acceptance of a published terms of use document.
A recurring access review of the guest users that asks each guest to confirm the confidentiality terms during each review cycle.
A Microsoft Entra ID Protection sign-in risk policy that requires MFA and shows the terms only when a guest's sign-in looks risky.

stem: A bank with Microsoft Entra ID P2 sees two kinds of ID Protection detections. Some accounts have leaked credentials found by Microsoft; some sign-ins come from anonymous IP addresses for accounts that are otherwise clean. The bank wants users to fix both situations themselves without waiting for administrators. Which TWO risk-based Conditional Access settings fit these two cases? (Select TWO)

choices.text: For medium sign-in risk, require a password change for every account in the tenant so that leaked passwords are replaced at once.
For high user risk, require MFA at each sign-in, because completing MFA proves the leaked password is still safe to keep using.
For any sign-in risk, block access permanently until an administrator deletes the account and creates a new one for the user.
For high user risk, require a secure password change so the user replaces the leaked password and the user risk is remediated.
For medium or high sign-in risk, require multifactor authentication so the user proves that the sign-in is legitimate.

stem: A retailer licensed for Microsoft Entra ID Governance moves dozens of employees between departments every month. When an employee's department attribute changes, IT wants that person's manager emailed and the person removed from the old department's groups automatically, without scripts. Joiners and leavers are already handled. Which capability covers this mover scenario with the LEAST custom work?

choices.text: A lifecycle workflow with a mover trigger on the department attribute that runs built-in tasks to notify the manager and remove groups.
A Privileged Identity Management policy that makes department group membership eligible and requires managers to approve each activation.
An access review of each department group every quarter so that managers remove people who have moved since the last review cycle.
A dynamic security group rule for each department that adds users by attribute, plus a weekly email the help desk sends to managers.

stem: Auditors found that users of a payroll SaaS app kept access long after changing roles. The company now runs quarterly access reviews in which managers confirm each user's access. Managers are busy and often ignore the review. Policy says access that nobody approves must be removed automatically when the review ends. Which access review settings meet the policy?

choices.text: Replace the review with a Conditional Access policy that blocks payroll app sign-ins from users who have not signed in recently.
Enable auto apply results to the resource, and set the option for users that reviewers don't respond to as remove access.
Keep auto apply off so that an administrator reads the results after each review and decides which accounts to remove by hand.
Set the option for users that reviewers don't respond to as no change, and send managers a reminder email halfway through.

stem: A retailer runs a hub-and-spoke network in Azure. It needs three outcomes. Public IP addresses must be protected from volumetric attacks, with Microsoft rapid response support and cost protection during an attack. Outbound internet traffic from every spoke must be filtered centrally by fully qualified domain name. Inside a spoke, only the app tier may reach the database tier. Which THREE services together meet these outcomes? (Select THREE)

choices.text: Azure Firewall in the hub, a managed stateful firewall whose application rules allow or deny outbound traffic by FQDN for all spokes.
Azure DDoS IP Protection on each public IP, which offers the same mitigation plus rapid response support and cost protection at lower cost.
Network security groups with FQDN-based outbound rules, which replace the need for a central firewall to filter internet traffic.
Azure Web Application Firewall on Application Gateway, which inspects outbound traffic from the spokes and filters it by FQDN.
Azure DDoS Network Protection on the virtual networks, which adds rapid response support and cost protection to automatic mitigation.
Network security groups on the subnets, with rules that allow only the app tier to reach the database port and deny other traffic.

stem: A national payments operator must keep its card-encryption keys in hardware security modules that are dedicated to the operator alone, validated to FIPS 140-3 Level 3, and fully managed by Microsoft so its staff do not patch or cluster HSM appliances. The keys are used by Azure services through the normal key management APIs. Which option meets the dedicated-hardware requirement?

choices.text: Azure Key Vault Standard, which encrypts keys with software libraries and lets many customers share the same multitenant service.
Azure Key Vault Premium, which offers HSM-protected keys on shared, multitenant HSMs that Microsoft operates for all its customers.
Storing the keys as secrets in Azure App Configuration, which encrypts its stored values at rest with keys held in Microsoft-managed HSMs.
Azure Key Vault Managed HSM, a fully managed, single-tenant HSM pool in which each instance is dedicated to one customer.

stem: An administrator adds an inbound NSG rule that allows HTTPS from the internet to a web VM. To lock things down, she also adds an outbound rule that denies all traffic to the internet from that subnet. A colleague warns that the outbound deny will block the web server's responses to visitors. How do network security groups handle the response traffic in this case?

choices.text: The outbound deny always wins over inbound rules, because NSGs evaluate deny rules before allow rules regardless of priority.
Responses are blocked until the administrator also adds an Azure Firewall rule that allows HTTPS replies to the internet.
NSGs are stateful, so return traffic for a connection allowed inbound is permitted without a matching outbound allow rule.
NSGs are stateless, so the administrator must add an outbound allow rule for each visitor's address and port range.

stem: A ticketing site runs behind Azure Application Gateway. During big concert sales it gets SQL injection attempts, floods of requests from a few countries where it does not sell tickets, and scraping by bad bots. The team wants protection at the HTTP layer, managed by Microsoft rule sets where possible, without changing the application code. Which service provides all three protections?

choices.text: Azure DDoS Network Protection on the virtual network, which inspects HTTP request bodies for SQL injection and blocks scraping bots.
Azure Web Application Firewall on Application Gateway, with managed rule sets, geo-filtering custom rules and bot protection rules.
Network security groups on the gateway subnet, with deny rules for the IP address ranges of each blocked country and for known bot user agents.
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session controls, which proxy every ticket buyer's session and block SQL injection in real time.

stem: A logistics firm uses only the free Foundational CSPM capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Cloud and wants to stay on it unless a requirement truly needs more. New requirements arrive: finding exploitable chains such as an internet-exposed VM that can reach a sensitive database, and assessing Azure resources against PCI DSS. Which TWO capabilities require the paid Defender CSPM plan? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Secure score, which aggregates the findings of Microsoft cloud security benchmark recommendations into one posture score.
Asset inventory, which lists the resources connected to Defender for Cloud together with their security posture and findings.
Attack path analysis, which finds chains of weaknesses that an attacker could exploit to reach critical resources.
Security recommendations based on the Microsoft cloud security benchmark, with remediation steps for each unhealthy resource.
Regulatory compliance assessments, which evaluate resources against standards such as PCI DSS beyond the default benchmark.

stem: A team wants a quick rise in its Defender for Cloud secure score before a board meeting. It remediates three of the four recommendations in the control for restricting management ports and also fixes a recommendation marked Preview. The score barely moves. The manager asks for the reason behind both results, citing how the secure score is calculated. Which explanation is correct?

choices.text: A control awards its points only when all its recommendations are remediated, and preview recommendations are excluded from the score.
The score measures the number of security alerts in the last 30 days, so fixing recommendations has no effect until alerts decline.
Secure score updates only after Microsoft auditors approve each individual fix, and preview recommendations count double once those auditors approve them.
Only recommendations from regulatory standards such as ISO 27001 affect the score, so fixes to benchmark recommendations never change it.

stem: A fintech stores payment API keys in Azure Key Vault. Its security posture is already reviewed weekly with Defender for Cloud recommendations. Now it wants alerts when the vault is accessed in unusual ways, such as from a TOR exit node or by an app that has never read those secrets before, even though the team has no security expertise. Which Defender for Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: Key Vault soft delete with a 90-day retention period, so that any secret deleted by an attacker can be recovered later.
A Foundational CSPM recommendation that checks whether soft delete and purge protection are enabled on every key vault in the subscriptions.
Azure Policy assignments that deny the creation of key vaults without private endpoints in the fintech's subscriptions.
The Microsoft Defender for Key Vault plan, a workload protection plan that detects unusual and potentially harmful access attempts.

stem: A university's SOC uses Microsoft Sentinel. Analysts want to spot users whose behavior suddenly differs from their own normal patterns, for example a spike in failed sign-ins or unusual data volumes. The team has no time to define thresholds per user, and it accepts that these results are leads for hunting rather than alerts. Which Microsoft Sentinel detection type fits?

choices.text: Scheduled analytics rules, which run a fixed KQL query at set intervals and create alerts when results cross a written threshold.
Anomaly rules, which use machine learning to learn a baseline of behavior over time and flag activity that deviates from it.
Microsoft security rules, which create incidents from alerts that other Microsoft security products have already generated.
Near-real-time analytics rules, which run a query every minute to create alerts as quickly as possible for a critical event.

stem: A SOC lead is planning next year's work for an organization that uses Microsoft Sentinel only in the Azure portal. She has read the official timeline and wants her plan to match it, including what changes for the correlation of alerts into incidents. Which TWO statements about Microsoft Sentinel and the Microsoft Defender portal are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Onboarding to the Defender portal turns off all automation rules, so every piece of incident automation must be rebuilt as Logic Apps playbooks.
The Defender portal hosts only Defender XDR data, so Sentinel analytics rules must stay in the Azure portal after onboarding.
After March 31, 2027, Microsoft Sentinel is no longer supported in the Azure portal and is available only in the Microsoft Defender portal.
Microsoft Sentinel is being retired, and its data connectors and analytics rules are moving into Microsoft Defender for Cloud.
After onboarding to the Defender portal, the Fusion rule is disabled and the Defender XDR engine correlates incidents instead.

stem: Data scientists in a bank's SOC want to apply their own Python machine learning models to Microsoft Sentinel data and to combine it with a risk dataset kept outside Sentinel on premises. The SOC manager wants this inside Sentinel's tooling, not in a separate export pipeline, and the results do not need to be dashboards. Which Microsoft Sentinel capability fits?

choices.text: Watchlists, which import a list such as high-value assets and correlate it with events by using KQL queries in Sentinel.
Livestream sessions, which run a hunting query continuously and notify the analyst when new matching events arrive.
Workbooks, which build interactive charts and tables from Sentinel data so that security managers can monitor trends and key metrics over time.
Jupyter notebooks, which run Python with machine learning libraries on Sentinel data and can bring in data sources outside Sentinel.

stem: A manufacturer licensed for the full Microsoft Defender XDR suite reviews three findings from one week. Domain controllers showed signs of a Golden Ticket attack. Employees uploaded design files to an unsanctioned cloud storage app. Several laptops ran a script that encrypted files in a ransomware-like way. Which THREE pairings of finding and Defender product are correct? (Select THREE)

choices.text: Defender for Cloud Apps for the unsanctioned storage app, because cloud discovery finds shadow IT apps and their usage.
Defender for Office 365 for the Golden Ticket activity, because forged Kerberos tickets are delivered to users inside email messages.
Defender for Identity for the unsanctioned storage app, because its sensors inspect web uploads from employee devices.
Defender for Cloud for the encrypting script on laptops, because its server plans protect end-user laptops in the office.
Defender for Identity for the Golden Ticket activity, because its domain controller sensors detect domain dominance techniques.
Defender for Endpoint for the encrypting script, because it detects and responds to malicious behavior on the laptops.

stem: A threat hunter in the Microsoft Defender portal uses advanced hunting across email, endpoint and identity data. An investigation needs data from seven months ago, but queries over the native Defender XDR tables return nothing that old. The company already plans to use Microsoft Sentinel. What explains the gap, and how can the hunter keep longer history for future hunts?

choices.text: Native Defender XDR data covers 30 days; onboarding a Sentinel workspace with longer analytics-tier retention keeps more.
Advanced hunting covers 180 days of native data, so the hunter must open a support case asking Microsoft to restore the deleted events.
Advanced hunting keeps only alerts and never raw events, so turning on Audit (Premium) is the way to retain the raw events.
Advanced hunting keeps data for one year, but queries older than 30 days must be written in SQL instead of in KQL.

stem: A media company has used a sanctioned Box tenant for three years. The CISO suspects that thousands of files already stored there are shared publicly or contain sensitive data. She wants them found and governed, for example by removing public links, without waiting for users to open or upload them again. Which Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps capability fits?

choices.text: Conditional Access app control, which proxies live user sessions and can block downloads while the users work in the app.
An app connector that uses the Box API to scan files already stored in the app and apply governance actions to them.
Marking Box as unsanctioned in the cloud app catalog, so that network devices block users from reaching the app at all.
Cloud discovery from firewall and proxy logs, which shows how much traffic users send to Box and other cloud apps.

stem: A CISO asks two questions. First, how well are the company's Microsoft 365 identities, devices and apps configured across Defender XDR products. Second, how well are its Azure subscriptions and AWS accounts configured against the Microsoft cloud security benchmark. She wants one posture metric for each question, from the tool designed for it. Which pairing is correct?

choices.text: The Defender for Cloud secure score for the first question, and the incident queue in Defender XDR for the second question.
Microsoft Secure Score in the Defender portal for both questions, because it reads the benchmark results from Azure and AWS.
Microsoft Secure Score in the Defender portal for the first question, and the Defender for Cloud secure score for the second.
Compliance score in Compliance Manager for the first question, and Microsoft Secure Score in the Defender portal for the second.

stem: A consulting firm already blocks malicious email attachments with Defender for Office 365 Plan 1. Last month a partner uploaded a weaponized spreadsheet to a shared Teams channel, and it spread through SharePoint and OneDrive before anyone noticed. The firm wants the same detonation-based protection for files in those workloads and will not buy a higher plan unless required. Which capability fits?

choices.text: Automated investigation and response from Threat Explorer, which is included in Plan 1 and quarantines files across all workloads.
Zero-hour auto purge for email, which removes malicious messages from Exchange mailboxes after the messages have been delivered.
Attack simulation training, which teaches employees to recognize weaponized files and is included only in Defender for Office 365 Plan 2.
Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Microsoft Teams, which Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 already includes.

stem: A vendor-risk analyst signs in to the Service Trust Portal with her company's Microsoft Entra work account. She has found Microsoft's latest SOC 2 report and a penetration test attestation, and she must not miss any later revision of either document during the year. She also wants both in one personal list rather than searching again. Which Service Trust Portal feature meets both needs?

choices.text: Create a Compliance Manager assessment for SOC 2, which downloads each new Microsoft audit report into the assessment.
Open the Resources for your Organization section, which automatically emails every user when a document in the portal changes.
Bookmark the Certifications, Regulations and Standards tile, which keeps the newest version of every listed document offline.
Save both documents to My Library and turn on notifications, so she gets an email when Microsoft updates a saved document.

stem: A health insurer's privacy board reviews a Microsoft cloud contract before it moves claims data to Microsoft 365. It asks for Microsoft's commitments in two areas: whether Microsoft may use the insurer's data for advertising or marketing research, and how data is protected while stored and while moving between services. Which statement matches Microsoft's published privacy principles in BOTH areas?

choices.text: Microsoft may use customer data for product advertising if it is anonymized, and encrypts data in transit only when customers request it.
Microsoft won't mine customer data for advertising or marketing research, and encrypts data at rest and in transit, such as with TLS.
Microsoft shares customer data with advertiser-supported services by default, and encrypts stored data only for regulated industries.
Microsoft hands customer data to authorities on request without notice, and relies on customers to encrypt all data stored in the cloud.

stem: A payments company must show PCI DSS compliance for two estates. One is its Azure virtual machines, storage accounts and SQL databases, already connected to Defender for Cloud with the paid Defender CSPM plan. The other is how Microsoft 365 data is handled, such as retention and DLP settings. The compliance lead wants each estate assessed in the tool built for it. Which pairing is correct?

choices.text: Microsoft Secure Score for the Azure resources, and Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance for the Microsoft 365 controls.
The Service Trust Portal for the Azure resources, and Microsoft Secure Score for tracking the Microsoft 365 PCI DSS controls.
Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance for the Azure resources, and Compliance Manager assessments for the Microsoft 365 controls.
Purview Compliance Manager for the Azure resources, and the Service Trust Portal for continuous automated testing of the Microsoft 365 controls.

stem: An external auditor asks a bank for two things before fieldwork starts: Microsoft's own independent audit report on its cloud services, and evidence of the bank's progress on the controls it is responsible for under the same regulation. The compliance manager wants to give each item from the Microsoft source designed for it, with no custom reporting. Which pairing fits?

choices.text: Download Microsoft's audit report from the Service Trust Portal, and show the bank's improvement actions in Compliance Manager.
Request Microsoft's audit report from the Purview audit log, and show the bank's progress in Microsoft Secure Score in Defender.
Export Microsoft's audit report from Defender for Cloud's secure score page, and show the bank's progress in Activity explorer.
Download Microsoft's audit report from Compliance Manager, and show the bank's progress in the Service Trust Portal's My Library.

stem: A law firm has two million documents already stored in SharePoint and OneDrive, many containing client account numbers. Most will never be opened again, yet each must carry the Confidential sensitivity label. The firm wants to test the impact first and does not want to depend on which Office version users have installed. Which approach fits?

choices.text: A service-side auto-labeling policy, run first in simulation mode, that labels matching files at rest in SharePoint and OneDrive.
A default sensitivity label in the label policy, which labels every unlabeled document the next time a user saves it in an Office app.
Client-side auto-labeling in Office apps, which applies or recommends the label when a user next edits each matching document.
A retention label policy that auto-applies a Confidential retention label to every file that contains client account numbers.

stem: A research institute starts a data protection program in Microsoft Purview. It needs to know right now where items that contain passport numbers are stored, to review which files had labels removed or downgraded during the last few weeks, and to recognize grant proposals, which have no fixed number pattern. Which THREE Purview capabilities meet these needs? (Select THREE)

choices.text: Activity explorer, which lists every file in SharePoint and OneDrive that currently contains passport numbers, whether or not it was touched.
A custom trainable classifier, which learns to recognize grant proposals from positive and negative sample documents.
Content explorer, which keeps a full year of history of labels removed or downgraded so the team can review them later.
A keyword-only sensitive information type, which recognizes grant proposals by matching the word proposal in the title.
Activity explorer, which shows a history of actions on labeled content, such as labels being removed or changed, over the last 30 days.
Content explorer, which shows a current snapshot of items with sensitive information types or labels and where they are stored.

stem: A document in an HR SharePoint site is covered by an org-wide retention policy that retains all site content for six years and then deletes it. An HR manager also applied a retention label that retains for two years and then deletes. A colleague expects the document to be deleted after two years. Using the principles of retention, when is it permanently deleted?

choices.text: After four years, because Purview averages the two retention periods when a policy and a label apply to the same item.
After two years, because a retention label is explicit and its delete action always wins over any retention policy's retention.
After six years, because the longest retention period wins, and the label's delete action applies only when that period ends.
Never automatically, because conflicting retention settings cancel each other out and an administrator must then delete the item by hand.

stem: In November, a company discovers that an attacker may have deleted SharePoint files and accessed mailboxes in March, eight months earlier. Its organization has only Audit (Standard), and searches for March activity return nothing. Leadership wants future investigations to reach back at least a year for Exchange, SharePoint and Microsoft Entra activity, with the least custom work. What should the company do?

choices.text: Turn on eDiscovery holds for all mailboxes and sites, so that the audit log keeps every related activity record for a year.
Stay on Audit (Standard) and change its default retention to one year for all records in the audit log search settings.
Create a retention policy for all Exchange mailboxes, which also extends how long the audit log keeps mailbox access records.
Move to Audit (Premium), whose default policy keeps Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint records for one year.

stem: A software company is considering Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management, but its works council wants proof of need before any policy monitors employees. Leadership asks for an early view of where potential insider risk may be higher across the organization, to decide which policy templates and scope to use. Which capability provides this view before any policy is created?

choices.text: The Data theft by departing users policy template, which starts scoring all employees as soon as an HR connector is configured.
An eDiscovery (Premium) case for every department, which collects all employees' mail and files for the works council to review.
Activity explorer, which shows the history of labeling activities so leadership can guess which users might take data.
Insider risk analytics, which evaluates potential insider risks across the organization without any insider risk policies.

stem: An engineering firm must send CAD archives of several gigabytes each to a manufacturing partner over the internet. The two firms have never exchanged a secret key and cannot meet to do so. The partner must be able to confirm that each archive really came from the engineering firm and was not altered in transit. The firm's architect adds that asymmetric algorithms are far slower than symmetric ones on large amounts of data, and transfers must stay fast. Which THREE steps together meet all of these requirements? (Select THREE)

choices.text: Encrypt each archive with a newly generated symmetric key, because symmetric encryption is fast on large amounts of data.
Encrypt each whole archive with the partner's public key, because asymmetric encryption is the only way to avoid exchanging a key first.
Encrypt the symmetric key with the engineering firm's own public key, so the partner can decrypt it later with that same public key.
Hash the archive and send only the hash value, because the partner can reverse the hash to rebuild any archive content that was changed.
Encrypt that symmetric key with the partner's public key, so only the partner's private key can recover the archive key.
Hash the archive and sign the hash with the firm's private key, so the partner can check it with the firm's public key.

stem: A payments startup designs three data stores. Customer passwords must be checked at every sign-in but must never be recoverable, not even by the company's own administrators. Card numbers must be stored so that the refunds service can later read the full number and send it to the card network. Archived log files must let auditors prove that a file has not changed since it was archived. In a design review, the security architect adds that two customers who happen to choose the same password must never produce the same stored value. Which design meets every requirement?

choices.text: Unsalted hashes for the passwords, salted hashes for the card numbers, and a digital certificate attached to each of the archived log files.
Salted hashes for the passwords, encryption with a managed key for the card numbers, and a stored hash of each archived log file.
Salted hashes for the passwords, salted hashes for the card numbers, and encryption of each log file so that nobody can read the archive later.
Encryption with a managed key for the passwords, salted hashes for the card numbers, and encryption of each archived log file instead.

stem: A distributor licenses every employee for Microsoft Entra ID P1 and reviews six security requirements before its budget meeting. Finance wants to know which requirements force an upgrade of some users to Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance, and which the current licenses already cover. The requirements protect administrators, guests, and hybrid employees who still sign in to on-premises PCs with passwords synchronized from Active Directory, so several features look advanced but are not. Which THREE requirements need capabilities that Microsoft Entra ID P1 does not include? (Select THREE)

choices.text: Require MFA for every user who signs in from outside the company's named locations, by using a Conditional Access policy for all apps.
Let hybrid employees reset forgotten passwords themselves and write each new password back to on-premises Active Directory at once.
Have managers recertify every quarter whether each guest still needs membership in the project groups, removing those who do not.
Require guests to accept a terms of use document through a Conditional Access grant control before they can open shared SharePoint sites.
Make administrators only eligible for Global Administrator and require approval and MFA every time one of them activates it.
Block sign-ins automatically when ID Protection rates the sign-in risk as high, by using a risk-based Conditional Access policy.

stem: A hospital's identity team writes three rules. Clinicians may open the electronic health record app only from devices that Intune reports as compliant. Any sign-in that Microsoft rates as coming from an anonymous IP address or with unfamiliar sign-in properties must be challenged with MFA, while ordinary sign-ins are not. The four engineers who manage Microsoft Entra settings must not hold the Privileged Role Administrator role between tasks; each use must be approved by the CISO and end automatically four hours later. The hospital has Microsoft Entra ID P2. Which combination of features fits all three rules?

choices.text: An Intune compliance policy alone for the app, security defaults for the risky sign-ins, and an entitlement management access package containing the role.
PIM for the health record app, a Conditional Access named location that lists anonymous IP addresses, and quarterly access reviews of the role.
Conditional Access requiring a compliant device, a user risk policy from ID Protection that forces a password change, and permanent active role assignments.
Conditional Access requiring a compliant device, a sign-in risk condition from ID Protection that requires MFA, and PIM eligible assignments with approval.

stem: A retailer's platform team must create, start and resize virtual machines in every subscription under its Retail management group, including subscriptions that will be added next year, but must not change virtual networks or grant access to anyone. Service desk members in the same team reset forgotten passwords for ordinary employees in Microsoft Entra ID, but must not create users, manage groups or reset passwords of higher-privileged administrators such as Global Administrators. The CISO insists on least privilege and on no maintenance work each time a subscription is added. Which assignments fit?

choices.text: Azure Owner at the Retail management group scope, and the Microsoft Entra Global Administrator role for each of the service desk members.
Virtual Machine Contributor at the Retail management group, and the Microsoft Entra Password Administrator role for the service desk.
Virtual Machine Contributor assigned as a Microsoft Entra role at tenant scope, and the Azure Reader role on users for password resets.
Azure Contributor on each existing subscription one by one, and the Microsoft Entra User Administrator role for the service desk members.

stem: A manufacturer federates its Microsoft Entra tenant with an aging AD FS farm that it wants to retire next year to cut server and certificate maintenance. The works council requires that on-premises account policies, such as sign-in hours and disabled accounts, are enforced at the moment of each cloud sign-in. The security team wants Microsoft Entra ID Protection to report users whose passwords appear in leaked credential lists. The network team adds that, after the change, no on-premises server may accept inbound connections from the internet. Which hybrid authentication design fits?

choices.text: Pass-through authentication with lightweight on-premises agents, plus password hash synchronization turned on for leaked credential detection.
Pass-through authentication on its own, because its agents forward each user's password hash to Microsoft Entra ID for the leaked credential checks.
Password hash synchronization as the only sign-in method, because Microsoft Entra ID enforces on-premises sign-in hours from the synchronized hashes.
Keep AD FS federation and add more Web Application Proxy servers, because federation is the only method that enforces on-premises account policies.

stem: A pharmaceutical company runs clinical trials with staff from three partner research organizations, each with its own Microsoft Entra tenant. Partner staff must request one bundle that contains a Teams team, a SharePoint site and a data app, and a sponsor in the company approves each request. Access must end after 180 days unless renewed, and the company's directory must not fill up with stale guest accounts. Most partner staff who will join next year do not yet exist in the company's directory, and IT cannot invite them in advance. Which approach fits?

choices.text: A Conditional Access policy for the three partner tenants that grants all three of the resources and then blocks every partner sign-in after 180 days.
Privileged Identity Management for Groups with eligible membership in one group that grants the team, the site and the data app.
An entitlement management access package whose policy admits the partners as connected organizations, with sponsor approval and 180-day expiry.
Invite every partner employee in advance as a B2B guest, add each guest to a dynamic group, and review that group every 180 days.

stem: After an adversary-in-the-middle phishing kit captured both passwords and Microsoft Authenticator approvals, a bank decides that its Microsoft Entra administrators must use only methods accepted by the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength in Conditional Access. Administrators work from bank-issued Windows laptops with a TPM, and when travelling they sometimes use a tablet browser into which they can plug or tap a hardware key. The bank's architects also refuse to build or run any new certificate infrastructure for this project. Which TWO methods should administrators register to satisfy the policy in both situations? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Hardware OATH tokens, which generate one-time codes away from the phone so that a phishing kit cannot capture the codes in transit.
Microsoft Authenticator phone sign-in, which counts as passwordless MFA and therefore also meets the phishing-resistant strength.
Windows Hello for Business on the bank-issued Windows laptops, which binds the credential to each laptop's TPM.
Certificate-based authentication with smart cards, which needs the bank to deploy and run a new public key infrastructure for administrators.
FIDO2 security keys, which the administrators plug in or tap over NFC when they work from the tablet browser.

stem: A logistics group asks which Microsoft product should own three needs. Its SOC must correlate on-premises firewall syslog, a third-party VPN's logs and Microsoft Entra sign-in logs, and run automated playbooks when an incident appears. Its cloud team needs misconfiguration findings and one posture score across Azure subscriptions and AWS accounts. Its endpoint team needs detection and response on 5,000 laptops. The SOC works only in the Azure portal today and is planning a design that must still be supported three years from now. Which assignment fits?

choices.text: Defender for Cloud for the SOC's syslog correlation, Microsoft Sentinel for the multicloud posture score, and Defender for Endpoint for the laptops.
Microsoft Sentinel, kept long term in the Azure portal, for the SOC, Defender for Cloud for the posture score, and Defender for Endpoint for laptops.
Defender XDR advanced hunting for the third-party syslog, Defender for Cloud Apps for the AWS posture, and Intune for detection on the laptops.
Microsoft Sentinel, planned for the Defender portal, for the SOC, Defender for Cloud for the posture score, and Defender for Endpoint for laptops.

stem: A law firm's analysts review three events in the Microsoft Defender portal. A lawyer clicked a link in a Microsoft Teams chat that led to a credential-harvesting page; the page was harmless when the message was sent and turned malicious later. A third-party app that a partner published received consent through OAuth to read every mailbox and is now pulling large volumes of mail. On premises, an account's NTLM hash was reused to authenticate to a file server and then to a domain controller. Which products are designed to detect or protect against these events, in this order?

choices.text: Defender for Office 365 Safe Links, Defender for Cloud Apps app governance, and Defender for Identity.
Defender for Office 365 Safe Attachments, Defender for Identity, and Defender for Cloud Apps session controls.
Defender for Endpoint network protection, Microsoft Entra ID Protection, and Defender for Office 365 anti-phishing.
Defender for Cloud Apps session controls, Defender for Office 365 anti-phishing, and Microsoft Entra ID Protection.

stem: A retailer has 300 Azure virtual machines and 120 Windows and Linux servers in its own datacenter. It already uses Foundational CSPM, and it now needs threat detection with endpoint detection and response plus vulnerability findings on all 420 servers, managed from Microsoft Defender for Cloud. The operations director insists that the datacenter servers stay on premises and are not migrated or rebuilt. Finance also asks to avoid paying for capabilities that do not protect servers. Which approach gives full Defender for Servers coverage for every machine?

choices.text: Enable only the Defender CSPM plan, because its agentless scanning also provides endpoint detection and response on Azure and on-premises servers.
Enable Defender for Servers on the subscriptions and onboard the datacenter servers as Azure Arc-enabled machines so the plan covers them too.
Enable Defender for Servers on the subscriptions only, because the plan discovers on-premises servers automatically through network scanning.
Migrate the datacenter servers to Azure virtual machines first, because Defender for Servers cannot protect any machines that run outside Azure.

stem: A SOC onboarded its Microsoft Sentinel workspace to the Microsoft Defender portal last month and also uses Defender XDR. Before onboarding it had three detections: a Microsoft security rule that created Sentinel incidents from Defender for Cloud Apps alerts, a scheduled rule for a custom firewall query, and a near-real-time rule for any sign-in by a break-glass account. An engineer now notices that one of these rules shows as disabled, although incidents for its alerts still appear. Which statement explains what changed and what now creates those incidents?

choices.text: Scheduled rules are disabled after onboarding, so the custom firewall query must be rewritten as a Defender XDR custom detection.
Microsoft security rules are disabled after onboarding, and Defender XDR now creates incidents for those Microsoft alerts instead.
Near-real-time rules are disabled after onboarding, so the break-glass detection must move to a Logic Apps playbook on a timer.
All Sentinel analytics rules are disabled after onboarding, and incidents now come only from Defender XDR's own built-in detections.

stem: A payment gateway that runs its workloads in Azure virtual networks must satisfy three findings from its auditors. All outbound traffic from its workloads to the internet must pass through one central, managed firewall that filters by fully qualified domain name. Outbound HTTPS must be decrypted and inspected, so that malware hidden in encrypted traffic is detected, together with signature-based intrusion detection and prevention. Inbound requests to the public payment API must be protected from SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Which design meets every finding?

choices.text: Network security groups with outbound service tags for the filtering, plus Azure DDoS Network Protection to stop inbound SQL injection.
Azure Firewall Standard in a hub for outbound FQDN filtering and threat intelligence, plus WAF on Application Gateway in front of the API.
Azure Firewall Basic in a hub for outbound filtering, plus network security groups that block SQL injection attempts to the API subnet.
Azure Firewall Premium in a hub for outbound TLS inspection and IDPS, plus WAF on Application Gateway in front of the payment API.

stem: A software company runs two apps in Azure App Service, Billing and Reporting. Each app must read only its own secrets from Azure Key Vault, and neither may ever read the other's. No credential may be stored in code or app settings, and Microsoft's Key Vault guidance should be followed instead of per-secret role assignments. A reviewer also notes that several platform engineers hold the Key Vault Contributor role to manage vault settings, and they must not be able to read any secret value. Which TWO measures meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Store a client secret for each app's own app registration in its App Service settings, and rotate both client secrets every 90 days.
Keep both apps' secrets in one shared vault and assign each app's identity Key Vault Secrets User on individual secrets, as Microsoft recommends.
Use the Azure RBAC permission model on the vaults, so Contributor holders cannot grant themselves data access through access policies.
Use vault access policies instead, because Key Vault Contributor is a data plane role that already lets engineers read every secret value.
Give each app a managed identity and assign it Key Vault Secrets User on a vault that only that app uses.

stem: A company has Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 on 6,000 Windows laptops, and Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 2 on 400 servers that are onboarded to Defender for Cloud. The security team must run security baselines assessments and browser extensions assessments on every device, laptops and servers alike, from Defender Vulnerability Management. Finance will approve new licenses only where they are strictly required, and the CISO wants one consistent set of vulnerability capabilities across both groups. Which licensing decision meets the requirement?

choices.text: Buy the Defender Vulnerability Management add-on for the laptops only, because Defender for Servers Plan 2 already unlocks the premium capabilities on servers.
Buy nothing, because Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 already includes security baselines and browser extensions assessment for every device.
Buy Defender for Servers Plan 2 for the laptops too, because that server plan is the only way to unlock premium vulnerability capabilities.
Buy the Defender Vulnerability Management add-on for all 6,400 devices, because neither Defender for Endpoint nor Defender for Servers includes premium capabilities.

stem: A defense contractor sets three rules for design files. Files marked as export-controlled must stay encrypted and readable only by employees, even after an engineer emails a copy to a supplier or saves it outside SharePoint. On the Windows engineering workstations, which are onboarded to Purview, users must be blocked from copying those files to USB drives or uploading them to restricted cloud storage domains. The files must be kept for ten years after creation and then deleted, and nobody may edit or delete them earlier. Which THREE Microsoft Purview capabilities together meet these rules? (Select THREE)

choices.text: A DLP policy scoped only to Exchange email, because DLP for email also blocks users from copying files to USB drives on their workstations.
A sensitivity label with only a visible watermark, because the marking prevents suppliers from opening a copy that an engineer emails to them.
An endpoint DLP policy for the onboarded Windows workstations that blocks copying to USB and uploads to restricted cloud domains.
A retention policy on the engineering site, because retention policies also encrypt files so only employees can open copies that leave the site.
A retention label that retains the files for ten years from creation, marks them as records, and then deletes them.
A sensitivity label with encryption that grants access only to employees, applied to the export-controlled design files.

stem: A bank's records team labels signed loan agreements stored in SharePoint. Once a file is labeled, its contents must not be edited or deleted during the seven-year retention period. Records staff occasionally label the wrong document by mistake, and in that case the site administrators must be able to remove the label. To keep up with volume, the label must be applied automatically whenever a file contains a loan agreement number, rather than by hand. Which retention label setting fits all of these needs?

choices.text: A standard retention label that doesn't mark items as a record, because standard labels block editing of the content during retention.
A retention label that marks items as a regulatory record, because only regulatory records block edits and deletion of a file's content.
A sensitivity label with encryption and read-only permissions, because read-only encryption also prevents deletion for all seven years.
A retention label that marks items as a record, applied through an auto-apply policy, so site admins can remove it if needed.

stem: A finance document in SharePoint is subject to three retention settings, all counted from the date the file was created. An org-wide retention policy for all sites deletes items after eight years and has no retain action. A second retention policy, scoped specifically to the finance site, retains items for six years and then deletes them. A finance clerk also applied a retention label that retains for four years and then deletes. An auditor asks exactly when this document will be permanently deleted. What is the outcome?

choices.text: It is kept for six years, the longest retention period, and then deleted because the label's delete action takes precedence over policies.
It is never deleted automatically, because the three different delete dates conflict and Purview waits for an administrator to decide.
It is deleted after eight years, because the org-wide policy covers every site and always takes precedence over policies scoped to one site.
It is deleted after four years, because a retention label is explicit and its delete action overrides every retention period from policies.

stem: A chip designer wants Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management to flag employees who download large numbers of SharePoint files or copy data to personal cloud storage in the weeks around their resignation. HR keeps resignation and last working dates in its own HR system, and Microsoft Entra accounts are deleted only 30 days after an employee leaves, which the team considers too late. When an alert shows clear theft, legal must be able to preserve and review the user's content for a lawsuit. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: A DLP policy that blocks downloads for users whose accounts are disabled, with its alerts exported to Audit (Standard) for the lawsuit evidence.
The Data theft by departing users template, an HR connector importing resignation dates, and escalation of confirmed cases to eDiscovery (Premium).
The Data theft by departing users template triggered by Microsoft Entra account deletion, with confirmed cases sent to Activity explorer for legal review.
The Data leaks template triggered by sensitivity label changes, with confirmed cases placed in a retention policy for legal's later review.

stem: A company receives notice of a lawsuit involving four employees. An org-wide retention policy permanently deletes email and OneDrive files three years after creation, and some relevant items will reach that age next month. Counsel needs the four employees' mailboxes and OneDrive accounts preserved for the whole case, regardless of other settings, and then wants the collected items reduced for review by grouping near-duplicates and email threads. Changing the org-wide policy would affect every other employee and is not allowed. Which TWO actions meet these needs? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add the collected items to a review set and use eDiscovery (Premium) analytics, such as near duplicate detection and email threading.
Run an Audit (Premium) search for the four employees, because audit records hold complete copies of their email messages and files.
Apply a sensitivity label with encryption to the employees' mailboxes, which blocks any deletion of their content until the label is removed again.
Change the org-wide retention policy so it deletes after ten years, which preserves the employees' content for any lawsuit length.
Create an eDiscovery case and place the four employees' mailboxes and OneDrive accounts on hold, which retention cannot override.
